requirement:
Colon-fenced directives and fenced code blocks have anonymous `block` nodes
with selectors under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
A block contains its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present.
Its parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.
An unclosed colon fence retains its block through the end of the enclosing
file or directive body, excluding the enclosing directive's closing fence.
rationale:
The reviewed tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. I did not request implementation source.

- **Anonymous `block` nodes with selectors.**
  - `fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` covers nested colon directives and a top-level code fence.
  - That test resolves every node's selector back to its index.
  - It asserts that block segments have the form `block@<12 chars>`.
  - It asserts that `node_lines` matches the byte range for each block.
  - `fn[anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates]` checks that selectors are stable and that duplicate blocks are numbered with `#1` and `#2` suffixes. Together these cover the `requirements.references.outline_selectors` citation.
- **Block spans the opening fence, body and closing fence.** The first test asserts the line ranges of the directive blocks and the code-fence block, and the byte range includes the closers. `fn[nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers]` checks closers with trailing text and whitespace. It also checks a `~~~` fence that contains `::::::` and `:::{fake}`, which stay literal. `fn[literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text]` checks that a code fence swallows directive-looking text into a single block.
- **Parent is the nearest enclosing container.**
  - The first test asserts parents for blocks and paragraphs under a section and under nested directives.
  - The nested-fence test asserts that both the inner directive and the `~~~` code block have the outer directive as parent.
  - `fn[unfinished_code_fences_remain_literal_blocks_through_eof]` asserts a parent of `section[H]`.
  - `fn[empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets]` covers nesting inside block quotes with CRLF line endings and Unicode text.
- **Unclosed colon fence.**
  - `fn[unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside]` covers an unclosed fence at end of file, both with and without a trailing newline. It also covers an unclosed fence after a heading and under a section, and it asserts that `byte_end` equals the source length.
  - The same test covers an unclosed inner `:::{tip}` inside a closed `::::::{note}`. The inner block ends before the outer closer, the outer closer is outside the inner block's text, and the inner block's parent is the outer block. A following paragraph is owned by the section rather than by either block.
  - `fn[unfinished_code_fences_remain_literal_blocks_through_eof]` covers the unclosed code-fence case through end of file.

I found no input class named by the text that goes untested, and no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept.
